characters.name: Akamaru
characters.canonical_version: Naruto/Shippuden manga continuity (provisional; primary manga unverified)
characters.justification: Kiba's ninken and combat partner. Sources show him fighting alongside Kiba (including Beast Human Clone teamwork against Naruto), being knocked out in the finals, and fighting Sakon and Ukon. He does not speak. Independent draft eligibility is uncertain because he is a companion animal rather than a clearly self-directed character, though he acts on his own initiative in sources.

evidence_leads.lead: Exam fights, finals knockout, and antidote episode; Sakon/Ukon battle
Inuzuka ninken roster and lifespan notes

characters.name: Pakkun
characters.canonical_version: Naruto/Shippuden manga continuity (provisional; primary manga unverified)
characters.justification: Kakashi's ninken and tracker. Sources describe him as a non-fighter whose smell-based tracking is his main value, and as a speaking, reasoning ninken who acts with autonomy. Support 3 reflects tracking and sensory assistance. Power 1 reflects the lack of combat evidence. Eligibility is stronger than Akamaru's because he speaks and reasons, but still needs a policy decision.

evidence_leads.lead: Non-fighter tracker; ninken status
Speech and autonomy versus Akamaru

characters.name: Gamakichi
characters.canonical_version: Naruto/Shippuden manga continuity (provisional; primary manga unverified)
characters.justification: Naruto's personal toad summon. Early in the series he was too small to be a major combatant. Secondary sources say he matured as an adult and became a dependable partner, with notable contributions to human-toad combination techniques (Wind Release: Toad Oil Flame Bullet). Sources note he has his own personality and independent judgement. Eligibility as an independent sentient summon needs policy review.

evidence_leads.lead: Development, Flame Bullet contribution, adult-stage growth
Comparative toad context (sibling roster)

characters.name: Gamahiro
characters.canonical_version: Naruto/Shippuden manga continuity (provisional; primary manga unverified)
characters.justification: Giant Mount Myoboku toad. Secondary sources show him being summoned by Jiraiya during the Konoha Crush and during Pain's Assault. He pinned large summons, used a stick to hold down the Six Paths' summons, and crushed morphed White Zetsu clones. Size is inconsistently depicted, so Power is conservative. Eligibility as an independent summon needs review.

evidence_leads.lead: Debut chapter 124; anime episode 73; Pain's Assault role; size inconsistency
Konoha Crush summoning and Pain's Assault role

characters.name: Gamaken
characters.canonical_version: Naruto/Shippuden manga continuity (provisional; primary manga unverified)
characters.justification: Giant Mount Myoboku toad, also called Ken. Sources describe him as quiet, clumsy and nervous, and say he spent much of his time commenting on his own weakness. He still fought Pain's Animal Path summons alongside Gamabunta and Gamahiro. Power 2 reflects the self-described weakness set against actual combat defeats. Eligibility as an independent summon needs review.

evidence_leads.lead: Personality, Pain's Assault role, Jiraiya summoning context
Defeat of Animal Path summons alongside Gamabunta and Gamahiro

characters.name: Sakon and Ukon
characters.canonical_version: Naruto/Shippuden manga continuity (provisional; primary manga unverified)
characters.justification: Single combined playable character under the working policy. Sakon is the usually active body and can extend limbs and merge with opponents. Ukon is stealthy, can dissolve into an enemy, and gives authority within the pair, but is weaker and tires quickly when separated. Power 3 reflects the pair's combined output. Source identities are kept for mapping.

evidence_leads.lead: Body-sharing mechanics, separation weakness; debut chapter 203 given
evidence_leads.source_note: Conflicts with chapter 115 on the file page

evidence_leads.lead: Level 2 cursed seal, stealth, taijutsu; debut chapter 115
